state.misconception_label: Believes f(x - a) translates the function up a units

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: What transformation maps the graph of \(y=f(x) \) to the graph of \( y=f(x-3) \). I got Translation by vector
\(
\left[\begin{array}{l}
0 \\
3
\end{array}\right]
\) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me explain the correct method, and then we will work through an example together. So, when we have \(f(x-a)\), it actually translates the function to the right by \(a\) units, not up. Let's go through an example to solidify this concept.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so it goes to the right, not up? That's confusing because I thought the number inside the brackets would affect the y-direction... Can you show me an example so I can see why it moves right instead of up?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me work through an example to clarify this concept further. Let's consider the function \( f(x) = x^2 \) and see how the graph of \( y = f(x-3) \) is related to the original function.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Yeah okay, so with f(x) = x², if I do f(x-3) = (x-3)², that means... um, I need to think about what values of x I'd need to plug in to get the same y-values as before? Like, would I need a bigger x now to get the same answer? Can you show me what actual points on the graph would be?
